## v1.278 — Kids added for your crew come looking
CI went red again on PR #95, this time on 3202fca: `country-club` failed in headless (7/10) of one of the two runs on
that head. The other run passed the same shard, so this was not a hang. The failing check was "every kid moves or
fires" in the Eighteenth. With the crew in it, that match's 3 v 3 is fitted to 6 v 6 (v1.275). Two of the six on their
side are kids the street adds, and the round-robin put Brooke on Jamie's spot by the pool, 55 m from your start. She
walked 0 m and fired 0 times in 60 s. Run here she did the same in 3 runs of 8; main, where she is not in the match,
passed 6 of 6. The cause is v1.152's rule. An enemy kid with aggression under 0.45 (Brooke is 0.35) only marches when
he can see you or when he is bored, and an enemy only gets bored when two or fewer are left on his side. In a match
of six that does not come for a long while, so a player would have had a kid hiding at the far end of the course for
most of the round. That is the same fault v1.184 fixed for allies (Michael: C on D.19).
- A kid the crew's numbers add to their side (`crewFill`, set in `crewSides` when their side is fitted to the match's
  number) now gets bored the way an ally does. After 25–30 s within 2 m without a line, he comes looking however
  many of his side are left. The match's own kids, Seth, kids crossing over to Seth and a crew kid's street
  stand-in keep v1.152's rule. Snipers, defenders, VIPs and taggers still hold as before.
- Matches the crew does not change have no `crewFill` kid, so they play exactly as before.
### Verified

  times; Garrett, the other added kid, walked 42–130 m. 1 more run green beside `last-kid` (under load).

## v1.279 — Pad button names in the hints, and the pad turns the workbench gun and the Loadout kid
Michael answered D.38's leftover with B (18 Oct): the hints, then the drags. With a pad in hand only the range bench
and the squad-order hint named pad buttons. Every other hint still named a key: the E prompt at every door and at the
shop, mirror, bed and board; the treehouse ladder's W / S / Space; the tutorial's WASD, Shift, both mouse buttons and
R; the ammo box (HOLD LMB TO RACK, CLICK TO FIRE, R TO FLIP, F TO FORFEIT), the jam and rack bars and the slot hint; and
the pause and forfeit buttons (ESC, F, ENTER). On the workbench and Loadout screens the pad could click but not turn the
gun or the kid.
- While the pad is in use, the hints name its buttons (`padWords`, `PAD_STATIC_HINTS`). E is A. The ladder says
  Stick ↑ climb, and on the ladder Stick ↑ up · Stick ↓ down · A let go. The tutorial says the Left Stick, Click L3,
  LT, Pull RT and X. The ammo box says HOLD RT TO RACK, RT TO FIRE, X TO FLIP and BACK TO FORFEIT. Pause shows RESUME
  START and FORFEIT BACK, and the forfeit question shows KEEP PLAYING B and FORFEIT A. Those are the buttons the pad
  already used for each (v1.241–v1.242).
- A real key press, a real mouse click, or the mouse moved more than 3 px puts every hint back on the keys, puts away
  the pad's cursor, and lets go of a held stick and sprint. The next touch of the pad turns them back. The pad's own
  clicks and key presses are synthetic events, so they never count as the keyboard.
- The drags: on the workbench the right stick's sideways push turns the gun, its up and down tilt it while the cursor
  is on the gun (elsewhere it still scrolls), and RT / LT zoom in and out, the same limits as the mouse's drag and
  wheel. The viewport's hint says so. On the Loadout screen the sideways push turns the kid, on top of his slow swing.
  Full stick is 2.4 rad/s. Parts were already mounted by clicking, so nothing else on the workbench needed the mouse.
### Verified
- `tests/pad-hints.test.mjs` (new). The bedroom's prompt reads "E Use the computer" with keys, "A Use the computer"
  with the pad, and E again after a real mouse move or a key press. At the ladder foot it reads "W climb" with keys and
  "Stick ↑ climb" with the pad, and climbing by the stick shows "Stick ↑ up · Stick ↓ down · A let go". With the pad
  the ammo box reads MAG EMPTY · BACK TO FORFEIT and the jam bar HOLD X. Start pauses with RESUME START / FORFEIT
  BACK, Back asks with KEEP PLAYING B / FORFEIT A, and a key press brings ESC, F, ENTER and HOLD R back. The tutorial's
  five steps name the Left Stick and L3, LT, Pull RT and X, and R again after a mouse move. On the workbench, half a
  second of full right stick turned the gun 1.20 rad and stopped its own turning. With the cursor on the gun the stick
  tilted it 0.20 → 0.68 rad, and RT took the zoom 0.90 → 0.45 and LT back to 0.90. On the Loadout screen a second of
  stick turned the kid 2.40 rad.
- The suites that read these hints or drive the pad pass: backyard-range, bedroom-settings, calendar, crew,
  forfeit-ask, front-door, gamepad, gamepad-screens, hats, ladder-prompt, loadout-gear, loadout-kid, pad-orders,
  pause-menu, pickup, pool-noodle, shorts, sneakers, squad-hud, texts, tops, under-parts, walkie, workbench-labels.
  The whole suite takes about five hours on one machine here, so the rest is left to CI's shards.

  without teammates. Michael's list didn't name them.

## v1.280 — Capture the flag: ten seconds at your base after a tag
Michael's D.47 (18 Oct): "Capture the Flag needs a respawn timer, where enemies/teammates cannot start shooting again
until they've been in their base for 10 seconds. The player should suffer the same penalty. You cannot move or shoot
after you get back to your base for 10 seconds." Before, a kid tagged in Flags on Bellfield walked back to his base and
redeployed the moment he got there (after at least a second out). You were put back at your start and could move and
fire at once, with 2 s in which nothing tagged you.
- A kid tagged in capture the flag still walks back to his base, hand up, as before. There he now waits
  `CTF_HOLD_SEC` (10 s), still out: he doesn't fire, can't take or return a flag, and nothing tags him. Then he
  redeploys as before. Allies and enemies alike.
- You come back at your start held for 10 s. You can look round, but W/A/S/D and the stick don't move you, and Space,
  the trigger and the pool noodle do nothing. You can't take or send home a flag, and nothing tags you. The flag box
  counts it down: "BACK AT YOUR BASE · PLAY IN 7", or, when a flag is on the move, the news with "· YOU PLAY IN 7"
  after it. The respawn's 2 s grace now starts as you are let go, not as you arrive. Without that, a kid at your base
  could tag you on your first step.
- Only capture the flag has the hold. The VIP matches, the Pickup Game and the Last Saturday keep their respawns as
  they were (D.48 and D.49 ask about those).
- `tests/ctf.test.mjs`'s played rounds wanted both flag runners to walk 150 m. With a 10 s wait per tag a round can
  now end on two flags well inside its 150 s: 0–2 at 67 s with Andrew tagged four times and 102 m walked. The bar is
  now a metre for each second played, which is still 150 m over a full round. Its HUD check (Mason has our flag, in
  red) failed while you were held, because the countdown had replaced the flag news. That is why the countdown now
  follows the news.
### Verified
- `tests/ctf-hold.test.mjs` (new), on Flags on Bellfield. Tagged, you came back at your start with a 10 s hold. Two
  seconds of W and D held moved you 0.00 m, Space didn't jump, the trigger fired 0 BBs, a BB didn't tag you, and the
  flag box read "BACK AT YOUR BASE · PLAY IN 8". At 9 s you were still held. At 10 s you were let go with 1.5–2 s of
  grace left, walked off, and the trigger fired. Mason (theirs) reached his base 6.95 s after his tag and played
  again at 16.95 s, a wait of 10.00 s. Evan (ours) arrived at 5.72 s and played again at 15.72 s. Neither fired, held
  a flag or could be tagged while he waited. Protect Ryan's respawn has no hold.
- `ctf` (with its two changes), `ctf-clock`, `bellfield`, `northcliff`, `crew-roster`, `crew-balance` and `squad-hud`
  pass. In ctf's kids-only rounds (you parked out of the fight) Andrew walked 128–242 m with 5–8 tags, and Mason
  267–488 m.
### Still open
- Whether 10 s at the base makes Flags on Bellfield drag, or lets one side run away with it, is for a playtest. With
  you parked out of the fight, the kids-only rounds went 0–2 to them at 67 s and 126 s, and 0–1 at 150 s.
- The 2 s grace after the hold is unchanged. How long it should be, and whether kids get one, is D.49 (in decisions).

## v1.283 — Notebook paper, part 1: the briefing and the result card
Michael asked (D.46, control room, 17 Oct) for every menu and card to look like pages a kid tore out of a school
notebook and wrote on. He picked A on 20 Oct (d66-notebook-paper): every menu and card goes on paper, and the in-match
HUD keeps its dark panels. He added that every line of text has to sit on the ruled lines, and that larger blocks like
the result card's boxes get a filled background so no lines show through them. The work goes one group of screens per
version, briefing first. This version does the briefing before BEGIN, the map's briefing popup and the result card.
- One shared look, `.nb-paper`. It is cream paper with light blue rules every 26 px (`--nb-rule`), a red margin, three
  binder holes and a ripped top edge. The edge is a CSS mask, so it holds on a card that scrolls. Writing is blue
  ballpoint in Patrick Hand, headings are black marker in Permanent Marker, and the buttons (`.nb-btn`) are yellow
  sticky notes outlined in pen, each tilted a little. Both fonts are embedded in index.html as base64 woff2, Latin only:
  24 KB and 30 KB, about 72 KB of text. Patrick Hand is SIL OFL and Permanent Marker is Apache 2.0. Nothing is fetched.
- How text stays on the rules. Inside a page every line box is one rule high, and every vertical margin, padding and
  fixed height is a whole number of rules. A smaller label inside a line (CASH, OBJECTIVE, BEST) gets a shorter
  line-height, so it can't make its line taller. Each rule is drawn 6 px above the bottom of its band, which is where
  the hand's baseline falls. The big marker headings (the outcome, the match name on the popup) take two rules and are
  nudged 2–3 px down onto the second one.
- Filled blocks: the EARNED box, the four stat boxes, the damage report, the objective and the field map. Each is
  filled with paper, outlined in pencil and a whole number of rules tall. The map is drawn 312 px tall (12 rules) with
  `object-fit: contain`, so it stays square. The damage figure's frame is 6 rules.
- A long roster (the Big Game's eleven rows) scrolls inside the page, and it scrolls a whole rule at a time (scroll
  snap). The page's height is rounded down to a whole number of rules (CSS `round()`, with a plain fallback), so
  scrolled to the end, the roster still sits on the rules. Before this the page ran off a 720 px screen.
- Colours on the paper: ink 12.4 : 1, pencil 8.2 : 1, red and green pen 6.2 : 1, marker 16.8 : 1. The light text
  colours the dark panels used (#9a8f7c and #ddd) are overridden on paper, including the damage list's inline grey.
  The pad's cursor used to ring what it would click in yellow, which would vanish on a sticky note. On paper it rings
  it in thick red dashes.
- Nothing else changes: the same elements, ids and handlers. Only classes were added in the HTML (`nb-paper`,
  `nb-btn`), and the HUD, the title, the map and the rest are untouched until their own versions.
### Verified
- `tests/notebook.test.mjs` (new; its helpers are in `tests/lib/notebook.mjs`). Both fonts load with nothing fetched
  from the network. It walks the baseline of every line of text on each page (outside the filled blocks and the
  buttons):
  - the popup: 11 lines
  - Bunratty's briefing: 19 lines
  - the Big Game's briefing: 43 lines, both at the top and scrolled to the end of its roster
  - the result card after a win: 11 lines
  - the result card after a loss with a three-hit damage report: 7 lines
  On every page the worst baseline is 2.5 px from a rule. Every filled block and button is a whole number of rules

## v1.290 — Tagged, you walk yourself home
Backlog D.48, Michael's B (20 Oct): "you walk yourself back, gun up, no firing, nothing tags you, an arrow points the
way". In the matches where you come back (capture the flag, the VIP matches, the Pickup Game and the Last Saturday) a
tag used to put you back at your start in one frame. Now you stay where you were tagged and walk home yourself:
- The gun swings up to point at the sky. You can't aim, fire or swing the noodle, and you can't take a flag.
- Nothing tags you, and no kid picks you as a target (`opposingCombatants` leaves you out), so nobody wastes BBs on
  you on the way.
- A panel at the top of the screen says BACK TO YOUR START with the distance, and an arrow turns to point at it.
- Within 2 m of your start you are back: the respawn's 2 s grace starts there, and in capture the flag the 10 s hold
  (v1.280) first. Lives refill at the tag (VIP and Flags) or stay spent (Pickup, Last Saturday), as before.
- Online play keeps the jump home, because a guest follows the host's word on where you are.
The respawn's grace and hold moved into `playerBackHome()`, and the walk is `startPlayerWalkHome()` and
`playerWalkHomeStep()` in `stepGame`.
### Verified
- `tests/vip.test.mjs` walks it in Protect Ryan. Tagged 8.5 m from the start, you stay 8.5 m out. A second BB tags
  nothing, the trigger fires nothing, ADS stays 0 and no kid has you as a target. The arrow reads ±3.14 rad with the
  start behind you and 0 with it ahead. The gun is fully up after half a second. Facing home and holding W, you are
  back in 2.83 s at 1.98 m, with 2.0 s of grace, the panel gone and the gun down. The next tag sends you walking again.
- The suites that tagged you and read the teleport now walk you home first: `ctf` (you drop the flag and walk from
  where you were), `ctf-hold`, `pickup-lives`, `last-saturday-lives` (its sprinting player turns and walks home before
  sprinting at the bulb again) and `pickup-fernando` (its player walks home before charging again). Fernando landed 11
  of 22 hits with the AK, no two lives inside 2 s.
- These suites pass: `vip`, `ctf`, `ctf-hold`, `ctf-clock`, `pickup-lives`, `pickup-clock`, `pickup-fernando`,
  `last-saturday`, `last-saturday-lives`, `damage-report`, `result-stats`, `online` and `smoke`.
### Still open
- Whether the walk home feels like a fair price is for a playtest. From the far side of a big map it can be 40 m or
  more, about 10 s.
- The gun's raised pose (pitched up 66°, lifted 7 cm) wants a look on screen with each gun.
- The grace itself is still 2 s, not ended by your shot: that is D.49, next.

## v1.291 — Spawn grace: 3 s, ended by your own shot, kids too
Backlog D.49, Michael's A (20 Oct): "3 s, ended early by your own shot; kids too". In the matches where you come back
you had 2 s after a respawn in which nothing tagged you, and kids had none. A kid standing over your start could empty
your lives as the 2 s ran out, and you could camp a kid's base the same way.
- Your grace is 3 s (`VIP_GRACE`). In capture the flag it starts as the 10 s hold ends, as before.
- Your own shot ends it at once (`doFire`), so it can't be used to attack.
- The panel at the top that pointed you home now counts it down: NOTHING TAGS YOU · 3 · TILL YOU FIRE. It stays off
  in the 0.8 s after a Pickup Game's clock runs out, which also sets a grace.
- Kids get the same. In a match where you come back (`comesBackMatch`: VIP, capture the flag, the Pickup Game and the
  Last Saturday), a kid who walks back to his base redeploys with 3 s in which a BB doesn't tag him. His own shot
  ends it (`spawnEnemyBB`). In the other team matches a kid's respawn is as it was.
- Online, your friend's kid gets the same 3 s as you (it shares `VIP_GRACE`).
### Verified
- `tests/vip.test.mjs`, Protect Ryan. Back home after the walk, you have 3.0 s of grace and the panel reads NOTHING
  TAGS YOU · 3 with no arrow. A BB in it tags nothing. Half a second later one shot fires, and it takes the grace to 0
  and the panel away. Owen, tagged, walks back in 2.9 s and redeploys with 3.0 s. A BB of yours in it leaves him on
  98 lives, and his own shot takes it to 0.
- `ctf-hold`: let go after the 10 s hold, the grace reads 3.0. `pickup-lives` and `last-saturday-lives`: 3 s of cover
  after a tag, and the next tag lands 3.08 s later. In their real rounds no two lives went inside 2 s.
- These suites pass: `vip`, `ctf`, `ctf-hold`, `ctf-clock`, `pickup-lives`, `pickup-clock`, `pickup-fernando`,
  `last-saturday`, `last-saturday-lives`, `damage-report`, `online`, `briefing-lives` and `smoke`.
### Still open
- Kids still aim at you in your grace and at each other in theirs. The BBs do nothing, but a kid can stand over your
  start and fire at you for the whole 3 s. Michael's C (keeping kids off a base in grace) is what would change that.
- Whether 3 s reaches cover from every start is for a playtest.

## v1.292 — An automatic fires no faster tapped than held
Backlog D.50, Michael's C (20 Oct): "fix the taps, then the 16-gun table for his OK before any change". This is the
fix. The table comes next, for his OK.
Automatics skip the semi-auto lockout on a fresh click (v1.20), and each click fired at once, whatever the gun's own
cycle. So the $55 Tick-Tock, which fires 2 BBs a second when held, fired a BB a click when tapped: 18 in 3 s at six
clicks a second. Every automatic but the Rattle Can could beat its held rate that way once clicked fast enough.
- A click inside the gun's cycle since its last shot now waits for it. The held stream picks up the time already gone
  and fires when the cycle is done. A click let go before then fires nothing.
- The time is counted as `_sinceShot` in `updateGun`, frame by frame the way the held stream counts its cycle, so a
  tap at the edge of the cycle lands on the same frame a held shot would.
  - Counted from the round's clock instead, taps at twelve a second still beat held on the fast guns: 36 against
    30 on the AK, because that clock is one frame behind the stream.
- A click that waits still makes the burst's jam roll, as a click that fires does (v1.250).
### Verified
- `tests/clear-guns.test.mjs` now fires every automatic for 3 s three ways, held and tapped at six and at twelve
  clicks a second (two frames down each).
  - held / six / twelve: Tick-Tock 6 / 6 / 6 (was 18 at six), Rattle Can 6 / 6 / 6, Clear Sprayer 19 / 18 / 18,
    Ghost Mini 30 / 18 / 24, Bucket Gun 22 / 18 / 18, AK and UMP 30 / 18 / 24, MP5 41 / 18 / 36,
    MAC-10 55 / 18 / 36.
  - Its held-rate checks reset the gun between tries. A try just after the last one's stream would now rightly wait
    out the cycle.
- These suites pass: `clear-guns`, `backyard-guns`, `burst-pose`, `gun-ak`, `gun-mac10`, `gun-mp5`, `gun-ump`,
  `gun-bucket`, `gamepad` and `smoke`.
### Still open
- The 16-gun balance table for Michael's OK (the rest of D.50's C). No price or rate changes until he has seen it.

## v1.293 — Owen stops standing inside Mitchell
The critic (21 Oct, Found in play): in Protect Ryan, after v1.282 kept everyone off Priya's cover, Owen moved in on
Mitchell instead, 1.8 m from her. Their centres were 0.01–0.17 m apart for 27–56 s of a 90 s round, in 4 of 8 rounds.
Reproduced here before the fix, 4 rounds of 90 s with you untouchable: 27.7 s in one round and 2.8 s in another. In
both, Owen had repositioned to the cover Mitchell held (`homeCover`). Both worked out the same spot behind it, so they
stood in one body.
- When a kid repositions, cover a living teammate already holds is left out, as long as any other cover is in reach
  (`teammateHoldsCover`). On a tight spot he still doubles up rather than freezing, as v1.67's defend rule does.
- This applies on every map, but only to the reposition pick. A dash out of fire and a bound pick as before.
  - In the check below Owen still ends up on Mitchell's cover by one of those for 0–9 s a round, standing apart
    along it, which looks like two kids behind one car.
### Verified
- Probe, 8 rounds of 90 s after the fix: Owen and Mitchell never shared a cover by the reposition pick. Their worst
  round had them within 0.35 m for 3.7 s, on neighbouring boxes of one car. Five rounds had none.
- `tests/vip-cover.test.mjs` adds 4 rounds of 90 s. Owen and Mitchell were within 0.35 m for 0.2, 0, 0 and 0.3 s;
  the check allows 6.
- These suites pass: `vip-cover`, `vip`, `cover-fire`, `idle-ally`, `bulb-sight` and the stuck-kid sweep of
  `bunratty_vip`, `lot_vip_night`, `bellfield_ctf` and `winnmark_ffa` (three ways each, 90 s).
### Still open

  (or `check`) will show whether a kid anywhere ends up exposed for want of one.
- Friday Night Lights' Nathan and Malik on one spot at their start (the critic's other bug) is a different cause: they
  stand where they spawn, before any cover is picked. Not taken this run.
- The critic's proposal of one rule that keeps every kid a body's width apart is still Michael's to promote.

## v1.294 — Aim held as a match ends stays in the match
Backlog B.12 (Michael, 21 Oct): hold aim as a game ends, go back to the room, and the view is still zoomed in.
Reproduced here: with the right button held to the end of a Bunratty match, the room came up at 55° instead of 75°,
and letting the button go there changed nothing. It stayed that way until the next match. Two things kept it:
- The right button's let-go counted only in a match (`mouseup`), so in the room the aim never came down.
- Nothing put the aim or the camera's field of view back when you came home (`enterBedroom`).
Now coming home sets the aim to none and the camera to your settings' field of view on the first frame, and the
right button let go anywhere lowers the aim. A pad's LT was already read by its state in a match, so it needed nothing.

  Before the fix the same steps left the room at the aimed angle (a throwaway check: 55° against 75°).

## v1.303 — Bunratty past its fence is the real place
Card `fable/d51-bunratty-hollow` (backlog D.51), step 1 of 5. Michael chose real scale (16 Oct), with each match fenced
to a part of the real street about today's size, and the two maps sharing an edge view (1A and 2A, 21 Oct). This step
builds the ground and the street past the fence. The 16 matches play on the same ground as before, and nothing inside
the box moved. Steps 2 to 5 are his house and the street's houses at real size, the Hollow's field on the river, the
28 matches re-anchored, and the edge views.
- **The street runs on to the fork.** Past the west entry the road climbs another 120 m to the fork with Sentinae Chase,
  bending west. That makes it 210 m from the fork to the bulb, as the real court is. The fork stands 13.6 m over the
  bulb (Michael: "more than 10 m"). Sentinae Chase crosses there, with a mown island in the Y, a black lantern lamp and
  a street sign. The road is the same ribbon with gutter and kerbs, laid at the same step along the curve, so the
  lane's samples from the entry to the bulb are the old ones.
- **The lots end at a bluff, and the woods fall to the river.** Past the south fence the ground keeps today's level
  for 3-7 m. Then it falls 22-24 m, at up to about 31°, to a floodplain. A 3 m clay cut drops to the water, which is
  ~190 m out from the bulb across the river's line. The guide puts the river 200-210 m SSE of the court's end. East of
  the bulb, the creek's ravine runs down to the river about 90 m out. The far bank climbs 52 m, with five big stucco
  and brick houses along its top facing the water. The mown field on the floodplain is the Hollow's, seen from above;
  step 3 builds it as a map.
- **The buried river is fixed** (Found in play, docs/refs/bunratty.md gap 7). The old plane at y −1.6 sat under 5-9 m
  of grass, with 16 far-bank trees buried to their crowns. All of it is gone. The new water is murky green-brown
  (0x5f6a4c, from the Chattahoochee guide), lies at −26 m in its channel and is clipped to the ground.
- **About 1,650 trees stand in the woods all round:** loblolly pines 14-21 m tall and hardwoods 12-18 m, with trunks
  clear well over head height. They are thinner on the riverbank, so the water shows through. The trees, the far-bank
  houses and the fork are one vertex-coloured mesh (two at night, for the lit windows), built by a new
  `buildMergedScenery` that the Hollow will use too. None of it is solid, and none of it stands within 6 m of the
  bounds. The ground under it browns to leaf litter past the tree walls and reddens at the clay cut. Inside the box
  the colour per vertex is 1, so the lawns in play look as they did.
- **The ground mesh grew** from 150 x 150 m to 600 x 500 m. Inside the old 150 m square it keeps the same grid
  (1.56 m), vertex for vertex. Past that the cells are 6 m.
- **The view reaches further.** Bunratty's day fog moved out from 35-82 m to 45-400 m. The camera's far plane is 450 m
  on this map (`viewFar` on the built scene) and goes back to 200 m in the bedroom and on every other map. Night is
  unchanged (fog 20-66 m).
- **Cover is unchanged.** The 80 random numbers the old far-bank trees drew are still drawn, so every match's cover
  lands where it did. The scenery uses its own seeded numbers.
- **The edge backdrop** (`EDGE_BACKDROPS.buildBunrattyCourtScene`) keeps only its north side: woods, then the backs of
  the Sentinae Chase houses, as the guide's gap 8 has it. The map now builds its own west, south and east.

## v1.304 — Michael's house and its terraces
Card `fable/d51-bunratty-hollow` (backlog D.51), step 2, first part. Michael's notes put most of the action at his house:
the front and back yards, and the driveway in front of the garage. The game had a small colonial there, 11 x 8 m. It
had no garage, no motor court and no pool, and a flat yard with a trampoline. This version builds the house at about
its real size from the guide (docs/refs/bunratty.md gaps 1-3 and its D.40 section). The play area runs south behind it
to take the terraces. The street's other houses keep their size for now.
- **The house.** A new `buildBunrattyHeroHouse` builds it. The main block is 15.7 x 12 m, two storeys at the front.
  It has cream stucco (0xd6c9ae), cream trim and a hipped dark-brown roof. A front cross gable stands over a three-light
  bay window. The entry tower is stacked stone, 3.8 m wide, and rises over the eaves with its own hip roof. It has an
  arched window over double wood doors, six steps up from the front walk, and a lantern either side. On the east end
  is the garage wing, 8 x 10 m, with three stained-wood doors (0x704723) and a carriage lantern between each pair.
  Its doors face north onto a concrete motor court that runs from the bulb's rim. The guide offered this or widening
  the whole east edge. The bulb's kerb now drops across the court, not where the old drive was. The house is baked into
  one mesh per material (about 20 draw calls). It collides as five boxes: the main block, the gable front, the bay,
  the tower and the garage.
- **The walk-out.** The ground behind the house is cut 3.2 m below the main floor (`bunrattyHeroCut`). From the deck
  down:
  - The white main-floor deck with its balustrade, on square posts. You walk under it. Its stair comes down along the
    garage's back wall.
  - The terrace, with French doors under the deck. The freeform pool (0x7ed1c7) and its spa sit on a pale pool deck
    inside a closed black fence 1.2 m high. BBs pass through it; bodies don't.
  - A stacked-stone wall (0x5c4b37, today's light grey was wrong), 1.1 m down to the lawn. A low parapet on the
    terrace side keeps you from stepping off it. Stone steps go down at the east end and a grass bank at the west.
  - The lawn, which falls another 1.2 m toward the woods and then drops away. It holds the trampoline (Michael: a
    trampoline, no playset) and a stone fire pit with its curved seat wall and pillar.

  West of the house, a side yard ramps down from the front lawn to the terrace. The neighbour's yard stays at its old
  height behind a stone lot-line wall, a 1 m parapet on his side. Every step in the ground lies on a line of the ground
  mesh's grid, under the house or a wall, so no ledge shows.

- **Cover and anchors.** Michael's yard props draw the same numbers as before. They now stand where the fights were:

the houses could not grow to full size without eating the yards the matches fight in. They grow as far as the lots
allow, and the street's look comes from the guide instead.
- **Six new houses** (`BR_NEIGHBOURS`, built by `buildBunrattyNeighbours`). Each keeps its old front line and grows
  back and sideways. Three of them have a two-bay garage wing, set 1.2 m back, with a concrete apron to the drive.
  | House | Style | Main block | Garage wing |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0 (north, Sean's) | grey-beige stucco | 13 x 10 m | 5.4 x 5 m |
  | 1 (north) | cream, columned portico | 15 x 10 m | — |
  | 2 (north) | tan-grey brick | 13 x 10 m | 6 x 6.5 m |
  | 3 (south) | cream stucco | 12 x 9.5 m | — |
  | 4 (south) | brick | 11 x 9 m | 5.5 x 5.5 m |
  | 5 (south, by Michael's) | grey-beige stucco | 10.8 x 9.5 m | — |

  The old houses were 8-9 x 7 m. The guide's three styles:
  - **Stucco:** French-eclectic, with heavy cream trim, quoins up the front corners, arched windows downstairs and a

  - **Brick:** white trim, twin front gables, and an arched portico with its own gable.
  - **Portico:** a two-storey portico on four columns under a balustrade.

  Every house has double wood doors under a lit fanlight, up a three-riser stoop, with lanterns either side. It has
  mulch beds along the front, a chimney, windows on all sides, and a back door with a step. All six are baked into one
  group: 22 draw calls together, where the colonials cost about 15 meshes each.
- **The north lawns bank up over the kerb** (gap 5d). From a metre past the asphalt they rise 1.4 m over 5.5 m, 21° at

## v1.306 — The range is Michael's backyard
Card `fable/d51-bunratty-hollow` (backlog D.51), step 2, last part: D.40's leftover. The range (v1.257) was laid out from
memory before any pictures came: a flat yard 25 x 31 m behind a small house, a board fence round it, a square pool on
one side. The guide's D.40 section (docs/refs/bunratty.md) describes the real one: a walk-out terrace under the main
deck, the pool in its black fence, a stacked-stone wall down to a lawn strip that falls toward the woods, the fire pit
at its upper end, and "the lawn strip is a natural lane, ~30-35 m from the fire-pit end to the hammock end, the stone
wall on one side and the drop on the other, with the woods as the backstop". v1.304 already built all of that for the
map, so the range now stands in it.
- **The same ground and the same house.** Bunratty's ground functions (`bunrattyGroundY` and its parts, and `BRH`, the
  house's levels) moved out of `buildBunrattyCourtScene` to the top level, unchanged, and the range builds
  `buildBunrattyHeroHouse` on them in the map's own coordinates. The trampoline became `buildBackyardTrampoline`,
  shared by both; the map still draws its one random number for its turn, so its cover lands where it did.
- **The way out.** You come out of the French doors onto the terrace under the deck, facing the pool. The way down is
  round the pool's fence and down the stone steps at the terrace's east end to the lawn, about 25 m to the bench.
- **The lane.** The bench (the same folding table) stands on the lawn past the fire pit, across the lane, and you shoot
  west along the lawn. The stone wall and the terrace are on your right, and the drop to the woods on your left. The
  targets are v1.257's (Michael: A), at the same distances: the six cans on their plank across two cinder blocks at
  8 m, the three bottles on a crate at 11, the two sheets of paper at 12.5 and 13.5, and the near bullseye on its easel
  at 15. The far bullseye is nailed to a tree at the hammock end, 20 m. A hammock hangs between that tree and another.
  The trampoline stands by the wall, out of the line (Michael: a trampoline, no playset). The targets face the bench,
  east, so the hit code checks the plane x = target, not z.
- **The lawn falls toward the woods,** so knocked cans and broken glass now come to rest on the ground under them
  (`range.restY`), not at y 0.
- **Past the lot:** the woods round it and down the bluff, the river and the far bank, the field below, and the
  neighbour's house over the lot-line wall. They are one merged mesh with nothing solid, by the map's rules: the
  map's tree spacing and thinning, and nothing within 6 m of the box. The camera sees 330 m and the fog runs 45-320 m,

## v1.307 — The Hollow on its river, below Bunratty
Card `fable/d51-bunratty-hollow` (backlog D.51), step 3, first part. Michael: "the Hollow's field was below Bunratty,
on its own river frontage; murky water, brush and logs; the WIZARD HOLLOW sign at the trailhead; from the field you
saw big houses up the far bank and a few houses against the river on the opposite (Dunwoody) bank". His answers of 21
Oct were 1A and 2A: each match keeps a today-sized play area, and the two maps share an edge view. So the field, its
forts, pallets, trees and the 12 matches stay exactly as they were, and the place round them is now the real one.
Before this, the Hollow ended in a cyan river 22 m wide and a flat strip of 26 trees across it.
- **The ground runs on** past the box, to the far bank and up the bluff (x −300..260, z −260..260). Inside 150 x 150 m
  the grid is the old one, vertex for vertex; past it the cells are 6 m. A new `hollowRealScale` adds the real place's
  terms, and every one is zero inside the box and on its tree ranks:
  - **West, the river.** Past the ranks' west end the bank's clay cut drops 2.4 m to the bed. The river runs 62 m
    wide (the guide says 70-100; the constants are in `HW`). The far bank rises from its own clay cut 46 m, up a
    slope of about 30°.
  - **East, the bluff.** The floodplain runs on 14 m past the ranks, then the bluff climbs 24 m to where the backs of
    the Bunratty houses stand.
  - The floor browns to leaf litter past the ranks, and the two cuts are red clay. The colour is per vertex, and it is
    1 in the field, so the field looks as it did.
- **The river is murky.** It is opaque, matt olive (0x3e4430), and reads close to the guide's #928f5c under the noon
  sun. It sits at −2.5, so the bank is 1.5 m over the water. The creek is a shade darker (it was the same cyan), and
  outside the box it now runs down to the lower river at its mouth instead of hanging at the old level. The shallows
  strip, the mud strip and the flat far-side strip are gone. The 26 far-side trees are still built, into a scene
  nothing draws, so every random number they drew is drawn and every match's woods land where they did.
- **The scenery past the box** is one merged mesh, two at night, with its own seeded numbers, and none of it is solid:
  - Floodplain woods up and down the river and on the bluff. They are tall hardwoods with clear trunks and about a
    fifth pines, in the guide's lighter canopy colours.
  - Thicket (Michael: "pretty thick" off the trails): about 175 shrubs with logs and grey deadfall, between the bounds
    and the tree ranks and east past them.
  - Shrubs along the top of the near bank, three driftwood piles, and a whole fallen tree lying out into the water,
    its crown bleached.
  - Across the river, eight big houses along the top of the far bank, facing the water. Three more stand down
    against the water, each with a dock on posts.
  - The trail: leaf-covered dirt on a mown verge, coming down the bluff from the east into the field at z 10. Deadfall
    and cut rounds are heaped along its sides.
- **The sign.** WIZARD HOLLOW is hand-lettered on a weathered grey board (0x979b91, from the photo). It is nailed at
  1.5 m to a big oak at the trail's head, 1.2 m past the east bounds, facing the field. The board is 0.8 x 0.2 m, a
  little bigger than the photo's 0.6 x 0.15, so it reads from the bounds.
- **The edge backdrop** (`EDGE_BACKDROPS.buildHollowScene`) keeps only its east side: the backs of the Bunratty houses
  along the top of the bluff, 66 m out, and the woods past them. The guide and Michael have no houses on the
  floodplain, so the north and south house bands are gone, and so is the west band (the map builds its own).
- **The view reaches further.** Day fog moved out from 40-120 m to 45-320 m, and the camera sees 350 m on this map.
  Night is unchanged (fog 14-58 m).
### Verified

## v1.308 — Logs and deadfall round the Hollow's field
Card `fable/d51-bunratty-hollow` (backlog D.51), step 3, second part: the brush and logs. Michael: "a lot more brush /
fallen logs / small to medium plants & bushes scattered around this area. It was relatively clear in this space, but
around the 'battlefield' and off of the main trails, it was pretty thick". v1.307 put the thicket past the bounds.
This version puts the guide's logs and deadfall (docs/refs/chattahoochee.md gap 1) into play, round the field's edge
only, so the middle where the fights are stays as clear as it was.
- **Ten fixed spots for logs and three for deadfall piles,** all in the ring between the field and the box's edge:
  - **Logs:** 4.5-5.5 m long, lying along x or z. They are 0.48 m high: crouch cover, and BBs stop on them.
  - **Deadfall:** a heap of grey branches, 3.2 x 2.4 m and 1.2 m high, with a soft surface.

  The trees are seeded per match, so each spot is taken only where it is clear. A spot is skipped unless it is:
  - 0.6 m from every trunk and piece of cover;
  - 3.5 m from every start and anchor;
  - 7 m from the forts;
  - 4.5 m from the creek.

  A match gets 4-8 pieces. They go on the end of `coverList`, so no placement's index moves.
- Nothing else in the field moved.
### Verified
- **All 12 Hollow matches were built on v1.307 and v1.308 in one run.** Every v1.307 obstacle is there to the
  millimetre, and 4-8 new ones were added per match (Juggernaut and the Ten-Way 4-5, the night matches up to 8). Your
  start is the same in every match. No page errors.
- **`tests/real-scale.test.mjs`:** the Hollow has logs and a deadfall pile, all at the field's edge, the nearest
  3.5 m or more from any start or anchor.
- **The AI suites on the Hollow pass:** `ffa-starts` (nobody in sight of anybody at the Ten-Way's starts), `kid-hold`,
  `cover-fire`, `hollow-held`, `hollow-fort`, `fort-spawn`, `idle-ally`, `spawn-facing`, `pickup-ffa` and
  `lot-hollow-polish`.
- **`idle-ally`:**
  - It failed once of four runs here. Rebecca walked 34.4 m on her own, but went 25.9 s idle without boredom.
  - That is correct play: each kid's threshold is drawn from 25-30 s, and she moved on before hers came. The check
    wanted boredom past 25 s, which disagrees with that threshold.
  - It now asks the same of 30 s, the fault it guards (an ally idle to 30 s and never bored), which the next check
    already bounds.
  - Three more runs on v1.308 pass. Three on v1.307 pass, with idle times of 25.3-29.1 s.
### Still open
- **Fewer pieces than the guide's 6-10 logs and 2-4 piles.** The seeded woods fill the edge, and a spot is skipped
  rather than moved. Whether there should be more, and whether the middle should get any, is a playtest call. Michael
  said the field was "relatively clear".
- **Ground, trees and match distances still to come.** The ground's colour and unevenness and the trees greyer and
  taller (the guide's gaps 2-3) would change how the field looks in play. Step 4 checks every match's distances
  (first contact, starts).

## v1.311 — Mitchell round house 5's corner
Card `fable/d51-bunratty-hollow` (backlog D.51), the fault v1.310 left before review: `tests/taggers.test.mjs` failed
on this branch since v1.305's bigger houses. In Bunratty Infection, Mitchell came down the 3.5 m side yard between
houses 4 and 5 and slid south along house 5's west wall (x 3.65) toward its corner at z 12.9, with the player 30 m east
and 12 m south. Only the south part of his step gets through a wall: 0.0197 m a step, just under the tagger's "no
progress" mark (`zStuckD`, 0.02). So he was counted wedged, and the wall-follow's sidestep, whose side was picked once at
random, pointed north, back up the wall. He reached z 13.6, a metre short of the corner, and went back, all round.
- **The fix:** on a fresh wedge, if the last step slid him along something (5 mm or more, and along the sidestep's line),
  the sidestep goes the way the slide was going. A tagger in a real dead end does not slide, so the old flip after
  0.5 s of no progress still gets him out of those. v1.310's tried fix (a lower stuck mark) is not used: it left Nick
  short in 1 round of 4.
- It is the taggers' own wall-follow only. The gunners' states and every map's layout are as before.

## v1.314 — Winnmark replayed: the place Seth leaves is filled
The critic's 22 Oct report (Found in play): once Lights Out (`winnmark_night_team_2v2`) is won, Seth turns rival and
crosses to their side (v1.275), and replaying a Winnmark team match with him you play alone. Lights Out and Two on Two
played 1 v 2, Outnumbered 1 v 3, while the briefing listed Jamie (or your crew kids) beside you. The cause is the one
the critic found: `crewSides` puts the kids it adds in a spare place copied from `slots[0] || kept[0]`, the match's own
allies. In these three matches Seth was the only ally, so with him gone both are empty. Each kid put there got an entry
with no anchor, and the scene builder dropped him.
- **The fix:** when Seth has turned and no other ally of the match's own is left, the spare place is the one he left
  (his anchor, `house2_backyard`). His VIP, role, start, behaviour, stats and team are stripped, as for any spare place.
  Where a match still has an ally of its own, nothing changes.

## v1.315 — The attack huddle spreads out
The critic's 22 Oct report (Found in play): in The Last Saturday with the first-time crew, Garrett, Colin, Brooke and
Trey start within 0.42 m of each other beside the car, Colin and Brooke 0.05 m apart. On screen it is one body with four
heads. v1.277's 1.4 m spread of crew-match starts leaves out the attack huddle, whose ring is its own. The ring is 1.4 m
across, and with 14 kids in the match its places are 0.63 m apart. Those that fall in cover are pushed out of it by
`findClearSpawn` along the same axis, so they land on one edge together.
- **The fix:** in a crew match (the match's sides differ from its own), each huddle kid's start keeps 0.75 m
  (`CREW_HUDDLE_GAP`) from the huddle starts already placed. `crewSpreadStart` takes the gap, and its search steps by
  the smaller of 0.75 m and the gap. The huddle stays where it was, and matches without the crew are untouched.

## v1.319 — Hold the South Fort: tagged attackers go back to the north fort
Backlog B.13, Michael's note (control room, 22 Oct): Hold the South Fort is "very very difficult". He offered two
fixes and asked for either: move the enemy spawn to the opposite base, "so that shooting an enemy has a greater effect /
longer cooldown before they can get involved again", or improve the fort. This version takes the first, for this match
only, as his note asked.
- **What was wrong:** the five attackers huddle at the east redoubt, 44 m from your fort. A tagged kid jogged back
  there and came again, and was back within 25 m of you 17.5-19.1 s after the tag. Over 90 s they spent 67-70
  attacker-seconds within 25 m of the fort.

  point, not to his own start, and comes again from there. Hold the South Fort sends them to `cluster_north`, behind
  the north fort and 65 m from yours.

    before, about 10 s in.

    the attackers spent 25-28 seconds near the fort in all. That is most of the match without a fight.

- **Hold the Fort (Night)** is unchanged. Michael's note named the day match.

## v1.320 — A hit bonus: 50¢ for every hit
Backlog D.59, Michael's note (control room, 22 Oct): "Can we have some sort of 'Bonus' system to give you extra $ in
each match? Like maybe you get an extra $0.50 per hit?" A match paid only its win or loss money: $2-$11 a win, from
`scaledReward`. Landing ten hits on the way to a loss paid the same as hiding.
- **The rule:** every hit you land on a kid of the other side pays 50¢ on top of the match's pay, won or lost
  (`HIT_BONUS`, `matchHitBonus`). Each hit on a kid is a tag, so the bonus counts the result screen's tags. A tag now
  records whether the kid was on the other side, so hits on your own team pay nothing.
- **Whole dollars:** cash has always been whole dollars, so the bonus pays $1 for every two hits and drops the odd
  50¢. Seven hits pay $3.
- **Where it pays nothing:** a forfeit, the tutorial's targets and a Pickup Game. The board's games pay "a little"
  ($3 a win), Michael's choice when it was built, and a 5-life 1v1 there would have paid more in bonus than the win.
- **Where you see it:**
  - On the result card, by the pay: "EARNED $7 + $3 hit bonus (7 hits) +$10".
  - On every ladder card of the map screen, after the pay: "WIN +$7 · LOSE +$2 · +50¢ A HIT".
### Verified
- **`tests/result-stats.test.mjs`, extended.** In Aisle Wars ($7 a win) you land five hits on their kids and one on
  each of your three:
  - The tags mark five as the other side's.
  - The win pays $9: $7 and a $2 bonus, the fifth 50¢ dropped. The card reads "$7 + $2 hit bonus (5 hits)" and +$9.
  - Six hits pay $3 in a loss, and nothing in a forfeit or a Pickup Game.
  - The map card has "+50¢ A HIT", and the tutorial's card does not.
  - The first section's one-tag win pays no bonus (half a dollar, dropped), so its IN REACH line is unchanged.
- **By eye:** the result card with seven hits, in the notebook style: the bonus reads in ink beside EARNED. The map
  cards at 1024x700, 1280x720 and 1920x1080: the pay line never runs under START or out of its card. At 1024 it wraps
  to two lines, as long pay lines already did.
- **These suites pass:** `result-stats`, `autosave`, `bellfield`, `ctf-clock`, `last-saturday`, `map-screen`,
  `notebook`, `one-ending`, `online`, `pickup`, `pickup-clock`, `pickup-ffa`, `pool-noodle`, `wallet`, `smoke`,
  `result-text`, `country-club`, `grocery-store`, `high-school`, `northcliff` and `sell-back`.
### Still open
- **For Michael:** whether 50¢ is right. A ladder win pays up to $20, and every 10 hits add $5,
  so the shop's guns come sooner. How many hits a real round lands is for a playtest. The amount is one number
  (`HIT_BONUS`).
- **Shown nowhere during the match.** The HUD's cash doesn't count the bonus as you go, and there is no hit marker
  yet (D.60, next).

## v1.321 — Hit markers
Backlog D.60, Michael's note (control room, 22 Oct): "I also think adding hit markers would be cool as well, to
confirm you were the one to hit someone." Before, the only sign of your own tag was the hit sound, and every tag
sounds the same, whoever's BB it was. In a team match you couldn't tell your tag from a teammate's.
- **The marker:** when your BB (or the noodle) tags a kid of the other side, a white X shows round the middle of the
  screen (`#hitMarker`, `showHitMarker`). It is four short strokes outside the reticle, so it hides nothing you aim
  at. It pops a little larger and fades over 0.3 s (`HIT_MARKER_SEC`), counted in game steps.
- **Red when he is out for good:** the X is red when the tag took his last life.
- **No marker for:**
  - a kid already out (walking back, or hand up);
  - a teammate;
  - a kid in his 3 s grace after coming back.
  None of those is a tag. Online, a tag on your friend's kid shows it too.
- **Hidden** when the match ends.
- **v1.320's comments** in `index.html` said v1.319. They now say v1.320.
### Verified
- **`tests/result-stats.test.mjs`, extended.** In Aisle Wars, with a real BB flown into each kid:
  - No marker shows before a hit. Tagging their kid shows a white X at full opacity, and 20 steps later it is gone.
  - Shooting the same kid again as he walks back out gives none, and neither does shooting your teammate.
  - Tagging a kid on his last life gives a red X, and his lives read 0.
- **By eye:** screenshots of the white and the red X over the Riverside Market lot. Both read clearly against the
  store front and a car.
- **These suites pass:** `result-stats`, `smoke`, `online`, `pool-noodle`, `squad-hud`, `notebook`, `vip`,
  `ctf-clock` and `out-shot`.
### Still open
- **For a playtest:** the size (40 px) and the 0.3 s. There is no sound of its own; the existing hit sound plays as
  before.

## v1.322 — A red flash when you're hit
Backlog D.62, Michael's note (control room, 22 Oct): "There should be a red 'flash' around the peripherals of the
player's view when they are hit ... The audio alone is not enough of a cue, as many bullets hitting near the player
can sound similar."
- **What was wrong:** there was a flash, but nobody could see it. A hit added a soft inset shadow (`#damageVignette`)
  and took it off 50 ms later, on a `setTimeout`, with a 0.05 s transition in. It was gone before it had shown.
- **The new flash:** a hit turns the edges of the view red. It is a radial band, clear in the middle 55% and dark red
  at the very edge, so the middle stays clear to aim through.
  - It starts at full strength and fades over 0.5 s of game time (`HURT_FLASH_SEC`, `hurtFlashStep`), so a hit is
    still on screen a quarter-second later. Its opacity is the square root of the time left, so it holds strong and
    then goes.
  - It runs on game steps, so pausing the game holds the flash.
  - It sits over the sniper scope's black mask, so a scoped player sees it too. It tints the HUD panels red while it
    lasts.
- **Only real hits flash.** A BB that doesn't count (your 3 s grace, walking home, the round already won) gives none,
  since only the hit that counts calls it. Online, a hit from your friend flashes too, as it already called it.
### Verified
- **`tests/damage-report.test.mjs`, extended.** In a Pickup Game with three lives, a real BB lands on you:
  - Before the hit nothing shows. On the hit the edges go to 0.98 opacity.
  - 0.2 s later it is at 0.75, and by 0.7 s it is gone.
  - It sits over the scope (z 7, the scope's mask 6).
  - A BB in your grace counts nothing and gives no flash.
- **By eye:** screenshots on the Riverside Market lot at the hit and a quarter-second after. The red band runs round
  all four edges at the hit, with the middle clear.
- **These suites pass:** `damage-report`, `smoke`, `online`, `notebook`, `vip`, `result-stats`, `pickup-clock` and
  `out-shot`.
### Still open
- **For a playtest:** strength and length (0.5 s; 0.9 opacity at the edge). There is no side to it: a hit from
  behind flashes the same as one from the front. Showing where a hit came from would be a separate idea.

## v1.323 — Spare mags are kept
Backlog B.14, Michael's note (control room, 22 Oct): "Buying and adding an extra magazine to a loadout slot causes the
magazine to be consumed/disappear once it's used in a match. It should persist between rounds and refill with
available BBs."
- **What was wrong:** a spare mag was built as a one-shot. The swap took one off your count of that mag and emptied
  its slot, so a mag bought for $ was gone after one reload. Its BBs also came from nowhere: the swap filled the gun to
  the spare's size without touching the bag, and the BBs left in the mag you pulled were lost.
- **Now a spare mag is gear you keep,** like a speed loader:
  - At BEGIN each spare mag in a slot that fits your gun loads from the bag (`fillSpareMagsFromBag`), after the gun's
    mag and the taped twin, before the speed loaders. It loads up to its size, or the gun's mag if that is smaller.
  - The swap trades mags. The fresh one goes in; the one you pulled goes in the pouch with what it had left. The slot
    stays, so you can swap back to it.
  - An empty spare mag dry-clicks, and the slot hint says it is empty. In a match the slot shows the BBs it holds
    ("Spare 10-rd Pistol Mag · 10").
  - At the end of the match whatever is left in them goes back in the bag (`returnSpareMagsToBag`), and the next match
    fills them again.
- **The words:** the slot, the loadout list and the shop no longer call it single-use or a consumable. The shop's
  header says "Yours to keep — carry one in a slot; it fills from your bag every match".
- **Mags already lost** in a save from before this build are not given back: the old swap took them off the count,
  and nothing records how many there were.
### Verified
- **`tests/wallet.test.mjs`, extended.** With the Spring Pistol (10-round mag), one 10-round spare mag in slot 2 and
  100 BBs in the bag:
  - BEGIN loads 10 in the gun and 10 in the spare, and leaves 80 in the bag.
  - With 3 left in the gun, the swap gives 10 in the gun and 3 in the slot. The mag is still in the slot, you still
    own one, and you hold the gun again.
  - A win puts 93 back in the bag: the 80, the gun's 10 and the slot's 3.
  - The next match fills the spare to 10 again (73 left in the bag).
  - A spare emptied to 0 dry-clicks: the gun keeps its 2, the slot stays.
- **These suites pass:** `wallet`, `fp-hands`, `gamepad`, `pad-orders`, `sell-back` and `smoke`.
### Still open
- **For a playtest:** whether the swap back to the pulled mag is welcome or confusing. A spare mag of a different size
  from your gun's mag holds the gun's mag after a swap, so a 10-round spare can read 15 once you swap a 20-round mag
  into the pouch. Nothing is lost either way.

## v1.326 — The Electric Pistol and the Electric Rifle
Backlog D.63, batch 1 (Michael: A), its second and third guns: "semi-auto rifles and pistols (electric)". Every
semi-auto gun in the game was a spring gun: a BB, then the slide, the pump, the bolt or the charging handle before the
next. These two have a battery to do that.
- **How they shoot:** a BB on every pull of the trigger, with nothing to cock between, as fast as a finger goes up to
  the gun's own cycle: 5 a second for the pistol, 6 for the rifle. Held down, the trigger fires one BB; they are not
  automatics. Run dry, the new mag is racked in once (the slide, the charging handle), as on every gun, and then it
  fires again a pull at a time.
  - The engine change is small: a spec can say `electric` with a `semiRPM`. After a shot an electric gun stays
    cocked and waits out its cycle instead of the spring guns' 0.25 s lockout and a cock.
  - Otherwise each shoots as its spring kin: the Electric Pistol as the Spring Pistol (its BB a little faster, 34 m/s
    against 30, and it moves you a hair slower, 1.12 against 1.15), the Electric Rifle as the Spring Assault Rifle,
    every number the same.
- **The shop:** the Electric Pistol is $110 under PISTOLS, after the Bolt Pistol, with an 18-round mag, a 30-round mag
  ($15) and a spare ($6). The Electric Rifle is $150 under RIFLES, after the FAMAS, with a 30-round mag, a 60-round
  mag ($20) and a spare ($10). Their pages say "Electric semi (a BB a pull, up to 5/s)" (or 6/s).
  - The prices are against their kin ($0 and $85): no cocking is worth a lot in a fight.
- **The models** are their kin's with a battery in them, so the grips, sights, hands and poses are the kin's:
  - The pistol has a tan frame and grip, a fire selector with a red dot on the left, and a black battery cap under
    the grip with a green charge light.
  - The rifle has tan furniture and a black mag, a battery box along the stock with its light, a fire selector, and
    a fluted sleeve that makes the barrel 10 cm longer, with the orange tip at its end.
  - The kids' blocky version of the rifle (your kid on the loadout screen, a friend online) is the AR's. The pistol
    is the pistol's.
### Verified
- **`tests/gun-electric.test.mjs`, new.** Each one is checked against its spring kin in Sean's match:
  - The shop: each under its kind with its picture, bought from its page for $110 and $150. The page says electric

  - Five pulls a second apart fire five BBs, and each gun stays cocked. The Spring Pistol and the Spring Assault

  - Pulled twenty times a second for 2 s: 4 a second from the pistol and 5 from the rifle, no faster than the cycle.

  - The last BB leaves it uncocked, and a rack on a full mag takes.
  - Aimed, the front post is 0.15° (pistol) and 0.42° (rifle) off the reticle. Both hands are on each gun.

## v1.327 — The Burst Rifle
Backlog D.63, batch 1 (Michael: A), its fourth gun: "burst rifles". The first gun in the game that fires a burst.
- **How it shoots:** every pull of the trigger fires three BBs, 1/12 s apart (720 a minute inside the burst). The
  burst finishes whether you hold the trigger or let it go, and a pull during the burst adds nothing. Held down, it
  fires one burst, not a stream. The next burst can start a quarter-second after the last BB, so a fast finger gets
  about two bursts a second, 7.5 BBs.
  - It is electric (v1.326's rule): nothing to cock between pulls. Run dry, a new mag is racked in once with the
    charging handle. If the mag runs out mid-burst, the burst stops there.
  - The engine change: a spec can say `burst: 3`. The first BB goes on the pull, and `updateGun` fires the rest at
    the gun's cycle. The burst stops if you put the gun away (a slot swap), it jams, the taped mags flip or the
    noodle swings.
  - Each BB is the Spring Assault Rifle's: 45 m/s, the same spread and curve. It moves you at 0.83 (the AR 0.85).
- **The shop:** $210 under RIFLES, after the Electric Rifle. It has a 90-round mag, a 150-round mag ($22) and a spare
  ($12). Its page says "3-round burst, a pull at a time (electric)". It is priced between the UMP ($170) and the
  AK-47 ($240), which streams 10 a second.
- **The model** is an electric M16A2 on the spring rifle's receiver, so the grip, the sights and the poses are the
  AR's:
  - The A2's fixed stock, which ends where the AR's does so it stays out of the aimed view.
  - The round ribbed handguard round the AR's square one, and no vertical foregrip; the off hand holds the
    handguard.
  - A grey mag, a fire selector with a red dot, and a green battery light.
  - The kids' blocky version is the AR's.
- **A test I had left red in v1.325:** `under-parts` counted 8 long guns and 8 short ones. It now counts 11 long guns
  (the FAMAS, the Electric Rifle and the Burst Rifle have the under-barrel slot) and 9 short ones (the Electric Pistol
  has none). The game was right; the count was stale.
### Verified
- **`tests/gun-electric.test.mjs`, extended:**
  - The shop: RIFLES reads Spring Assault Rifle, FAMAS, Electric Rifle, Burst Rifle, Spring Sniper Rifle. The Burst
    Rifle has its picture, is bought for $210, and its page says 3-round burst.
  - In Sean's match, a two-frame pull fires 3 BBs, the third 10 frames after the first.
  - Held down 2 s it fires 3. A second pull inside the burst gives 3, not 6.
  - Pulled every 3 frames for 2 s, it fires 7.5 a second and stays cocked.
  - With 2 left, a pull fires the 2, and the gun wants a rack; the rack takes. A slot swap right after the pull stops
    the burst at 1.
  - Aimed, the front post is 0.43° off the reticle. Both hands are on it.
- **Updated for 20 guns:** `gun-parts` (60 parts, none loose), `shop-gun-kinds` (RIFLES 5), `shop-pics` (20 distinct
  pictures), `backyard-guns`, `under-parts` (above). `fp-hands` and `loadout-kid` check the Burst Rifle too.
- **These suites pass:** `gun-electric`, `gun-parts`, `fp-hands`, `shop-gun-kinds`, `shop-pics`, `shop-tabs`,
  `backyard-guns`, `loadout-kid`, `under-parts`, `workbench-labels` and `smoke`.
### Still open
- **For a playtest:** whether three BBs a pull at $210 sits right between the Electric Rifle ($150, 6 a second
  clicked) and the AK-47.
- **For Michael's eye:** `tests/out/gun-burst-side.png`.
- **Batch 1 still owes** the semi-auto shotgun.

## v1.330 — BBs five times cheaper, in tubes, bottles and bags
Backlog D.66, Michael's answer B (control room, 23 Oct): five times cheaper. His note: "you can pretty commonly (even
today) buy like 2000-4000 rounds for like 15 bucks... 500 BBs should be a little plastic cylinder with a little
spigot/dispenser, 1000-2000 could be just tall cylinders (look almost like a coke bottle), and anything above 2,000
could be in bags."
- **The prices:** 100 for $1 (was $5), 500 for $4 (was $20), 2,000 for $14 (was $70), 5,000 for $30 (was $150). That
  is 0.6-1¢ a BB, where it was 3-5¢. A 350-round AK drum now costs about $2-$4 to fill from the bag, where it cost
  $10-$18, against $2-$20 for a win.
- **The packs and their pictures,** drawn in the shop as before from models:
  - 100: a short clear tube with a yellow screw cap ("100 BBs (tube)").
  - 500: a clear tube with a blue cap and a spigot tipped up off it, with its flip lid ("500 BBs (dispenser)").
  - 2,000: a tall clear bottle like a soda bottle, with a shoulder, a neck, a red cap and a label round it ("2,000
    BBs (bottle)").
  - 5,000: a big flat foil bag the size of a book, with a sealed strip and a hang hole at the top, a label, and a
    window full of BBs ("5,000 BBs (bag)").
  - Each container shows the BBs through the plastic. The descriptions say what each is.
- Nothing else costs BBs differently: the bag, the mags and the loaders work as before.
### Verified
- **`tests/shop-tabs.test.mjs`, extended:** the four packs are `100 BBs (tube)` $1, `500 BBs (dispenser)` $4,
  `2,000 BBs (bottle)` $14 and `5,000 BBs (bag)` $30. With $20 and an empty bag, the bottle leaves $6 and 2,000 BBs.
- **`tests/shop-pics.test.mjs`:** four distinct pictures at 112 px. The tube fills 61% of its square, the dispenser
  44%, the bottle 33% and the bag 59%; each runs at least 86% of the way top to bottom. The bottle's rule is now over
  20% (the packs' is 30%), since a soda bottle is narrow by design; it fills 33%.
- **These suites pass:** `shop-tabs`, `shop-pics`, `autosave` (it buys the 100 tube) and `smoke`. A picture of the
  four is in `tests/out/bb-packs.png`.

## v1.332 — Online: a tag walks you home, and your friend's shots are heard
Backlog B.15, Michael's note (control room, 23 Oct) after playing his brother online: "getting shot should leverage the
new 'return to your base' system; and I did not hear audio of my brother's shots passing by me or impacting near me,
all of his sounds were nearly silent."
- **The walk home.** Online play had kept the old jump: a tag put you back at your start in one frame, because v1.290
  left it out ("its guest follows the host's word on where you are"). Now a tag online works as it does in a Pickup
  Game against kids. You walk yourself home, gun up, with the arrow and BACK TO YOUR START · N m at the top. You can't
  aim or fire, and nothing tags you on the way. At your start the 2 s grace starts, as before.
  - Each game now says in its ~30-a-second message whether its player is walking home or in his grace (`g`). The other
    game shows him walking with his gun up in the air, as a tagged kid holds his.
  - The host's game is the referee, and it tags nobody who is walking home or in his grace. It no longer moves the
    guest's kid back to his start when it tags him: the guest walks there, and the host sees him walk.
  - A shot from a player walking home is dropped. His own game won't fire one anyway.
- **His shots.** Your friend's shot arrived and flew, but it played no sound: `netSpawnShot` built the BB and never
  called `playShot`. A kid's shot plays one from where he stands (`spawnEnemyBB`). Now your friend's shot is heard from
  where he is, panned and fading with distance like a kid's. The whistle of a BB going past you and the sound of it
  landing already played for every BB, his too, so the gunshot was the missing piece. A whistle with no shot before it
  is easy to miss, which may be why all of it sounded nearly silent.
### Verified
- **`tests/online.test.mjs`, extended** (two headless games over the stub transport):
  - The guest's shot is heard on the host's screen, 0.39 m from where the host sees the guest.
  - Tagged, the host walks home: `_goingHome` is set, the arrow reads BACK TO YOUR START · 5 m, and the guest sees him
    with his gun all the way up (`g` 2, raise 1). Three more shots from the guest tag nothing.
  - Put a step from his start, the host is back and in his grace.
  - The same from the other side: the guest walks home and the host sees him gun up. Three shots from the host tag
    nothing, and back at his start the host sees him there to within 0 cm.
  - The rest of the suite holds: the lives agree on both screens, the last tag ends it for both, nothing is paid, and a
    dropped friend ends it cleanly. 21 of 21 checks.
- **These suites pass:** `online`, `smoke`, `pickup-lives`, `vip`, `vip-spawn`. `vip-cover` is flaky in this
  container, and not from this change: Owen and Mitchell stood together 18-46 s in one round of four in 2 of 4 runs
  here, and in 1 of 2 runs on main's code (24.5 s). Offline, none of this change's code runs. It is filed under Found
  in play.
### Still open
- **For a playtest with your brother:** whether his shots are now loud enough at 20-30 m. They are as loud as a kid's
  at the same distance. Over a real connection the walk home may lag a frame or two on the other screen, as his
  steps do.

## v1.333 — Your own body when you look down
Backlog B.16, Michael's note (control room, 23 Oct): "Looking down in game shows nothing, but the walkie talkie is
visible and shows as floating. Can we just add the whole body mesh to the first person view?" The walkie had hung at
your hip on its own since v1.149, with nothing under it.
- **The body.** In a match your own kid now stands under the camera, built as the Loadout kid is: your look from the
  mirror (height, build, shirt or top, jeans or shorts, sneakers), the gear you wear (chest rig or plate carrier, knee
  pads, the belt and holster, gear shoes) and the walkie on its belt. The head, with the face, hair, hat and eye pro,
  is hidden, and so are the arms and the kid's own gun: the hands holding your gun are the view's, as before. The body
  casts no shadow, since a headless one would follow you round.
- **Where it stands.** Its eyes are held at the camera: the kid is stretched to your eye height (1.35 m standing, 6%
  over the kid's own 1.27 m). It stands 12 cm behind the eye looking ahead and slides back to 32 cm looking straight
  down, so you see your belly, belt and shoes past it rather than the top of your shoulders. Crouched or sliding, it
  crouches as the kids do (legs bent, body leaning in) and squashes the rest of the way, so the shoes stay on the
  ground and the torso stays under the lower eye.
- **It walks.** The legs walk in the kids' planted-foot gait (v1.171) at your real speed, forward, back or sideways,
  and stop when you do. A jump to a new place (a respawn) is not read as a step.
- **Your look.** A new look or new gear is put on the body at the next match.
### Verified
- **`tests/walkie.test.mjs`, extended:**
  - The walkie is the body's, on its belt. Legs, shoes and torso show; head, neck, hair, the arms and the kid's gun
    don't; no part casts a shadow.
  - Looking ahead none of the body is on screen, and the torso's top is 0.21 m under the eye.
  - Looking down (75°) both shoes and the torso are on screen, and the soles sit on the ground (0 cm).
  - Crouched, the soles stay on the ground and the torso's top drops from 1.14 m to 0.65 m, under the 0.8 m eye.
  - Walking, the left leg swings through 1.2 rad and the soles stay on the ground.
  - A new shirt colour is on the body when it is set up again, and there is one body, not two.
  - The walkie's old checks hold: out of view ahead, on your left at the hip (0.59 m up), in view looking down, lower
    crouched, with you walking. Looking down it is now 17 cm behind the eye rather than in front, with the body.
- **These suites pass:** `walkie`, `walkie-callouts`, `smoke`, `online`, `settings`, `grip`, `mirror`, `loadout-gear`,
  `pickup-lives` and `gait`. `fp-hands` passed its first 91 checks with none failing before this container's 10-minute
  limit stopped it; three suites run side by side here crashed or timed out a browser tab and passed alone.
### Still open
- **For a playtest:** whether the body reads right at a glance: how far back it sits when you look down, whether the
  stretched kid looks too long in the leg, and the crouch, which squashes the body by up to a third to keep your feet
  on the ground. The gun in your hands can pass through the chest when you look straight down, as in most shooters.

Backlog D.65, Michael's answer A (23 Oct): one list of every slot. His note: "list all equipment slots available, and

picker, but eye pro, armor and shoes sat in a separate WORN GEAR section with "No armor owned" and nothing to click.

## v1.337 — Lend your crew a gun
Backlog D.28 step 4 (card fable/d28-handmedowns), Michael's answer A on "Hand-me-downs and the BB rule" (24 Oct): a loan
at the loadout, a capped load from your bag, eyes and feet only. His spec: "you give a crew kid a gun you own (your old
one goes to Nick when you buy better)... A kid on his own gun brings his own BBs; a kid on a gun you handed him uses
yours." The measurement that came first (decisions, 24 Oct): an AK kid fires about 100 BBs a minute, an MP5 or rifle kid
15-25, so an uncapped AK in a kid's hands could cost a long match 1,100 of your BBs.
- **Where.** The Loadout's list gets a YOUR CREW part under your slots: a row for each kid in your crew with the gun
  he carries ("Diego · AK-47 · your gun, your BBs", or "his own gun and BBs") and what of yours he has on. A click lists
  his own gun first, then every gun you own that you aren't carrying, each with what it costs you a match ("700 of your
  BBs a match"), then his eyes and feet: what you own and aren't wearing, or "Take back the ...". A gun another kid has
  passes from him ("from Diego"). The briefing's lineup shows the gun as before.
- **It comes back.** You own one of each, so what a kid has isn't yours to carry until you take it back, free. Picking
  it as your own gun (the Loadout's gun picker, the workbench, the shop's EQUIP, which reads "TAKE BACK FROM ALEX")
  takes it back, and each says who has it first. Selling a gun a kid has is refused until you take it back. The gun you
  carry and what you wear can't be lent.
- **His BBs.** At BEGIN, after your own gun, mags and loaders have loaded, a kid on your gun loads from what the bag has
  left: two of its mags at your mag upgrades (an AK 700 or 1,000, an MP5 300 or 400, a spring rifle 50 or 80). Each BB
  he fires is counted; what he hasn't fired goes back in the bag at the end, as yours does. Out of them, he goes back to
  his own gun (its model swapped into his hands) and his own BBs for the rest of the match. With the bag empty he
  starts on his own gun, and the briefing already shows it. A benched kid takes nothing. A match a kid plays on your
  gun counts toward its sell-back count, as your own matches do.
- **Gear.** Eyewear gives him +0.05 aim (Sean 0.60 to 0.65), shoes +5% speed; it's on his profile for the match only,
  and he doesn't wear it on his model yet. No armor.
- **Your old gun.** Buying a gun with Nick in your crew asks under it "Give your AK-47 to Nick?" YES / KEEP IT, saying
  what he'd carry it instead of. YES lends it to him as the Loadout would.
- **Saves.** `crewGear` in the save: { kid: { gun, eyewear, shoes } }. An old save has none and plays as today.
### Verified
- **`tests/crew-gear.test.mjs`, new** (a save rule and a rule of play the BB counts lean on):
  - The Spring Pistol you carry can't be lent; Diego takes your AK-47, Sean your smoke goggles, Nick your trail shoes;
    the AK can't be sold while Diego has it; all three survive a save and reload.
  - The Big Game's setup: Diego on the AK-47 as a loan, Eric on his own MP5; Sean's aim 0.65, Nick's speed 0.85 to 0.8925.
  - A 5,000 bag at BEGIN: you load 10, Diego 700, nobody else draws (4,290 left). In a minute he fired 75-113 of them
    (four runs) and the bag ended at 5,000 less exactly what he fired.
  - A 40 bag: you 10, Diego the last 30; he runs dry, is back on his MP5 (its model's pieces in his gun group) and the
    bag ends at 10. A 10 bag: he starts on his MP5. An empty bag: the setup already has him on it. Benched: the bag

  - The Loadout lists five crew rows; Sean's picker starts with his own AK-47 and takes the goggles back; lending Alex
